key_insight: The paper reframes safety in meta-reinforcement learning as a reachability problem in information space, combining physical state and task belief to estimate the chance of avoiding unsafe regions indefinitely.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to build adaptive RL systems that can learn new tasks while explicitly enforcing safety constraints during deployment.
method: Define an information-space safety value function over state + belief about the task.
Show the value function satisfies a self-consistency condition and Bellman equation, enabling learning via meta-RL.
Use the learned safety value for safety filtering and constrained policy optimization during adaptation.
evidence_signal: Experiments on meta-RL benchmarks are reported to show the proposed safe meta-RL method is effective.
watch_item: Safety depends on accurately modeling belief over tasks; if the task inference or value estimation is poor, the safety filter may be overly conservative or miss hazards.
paper_title: Safe Meta-Reinforcement Learning via Information Space Reachability
